metric_definition: z-score composite = sum(w_i * (x_i-mean_i)/std_i); thresholds = TRAIN composite tertiles
limitations: config status is 'provisional_NOT_frozen'; thresholds and weights are candidate, NOT expert-validated; must not be adjusted using any XAI result (explicit rule in the config).

statement: Equal-weight composite scoring is not refit on VALID; the same TRAIN-derived normalization/weights/thresholds are applied to VALID feature values as-is.
metric_definition: n/a (design decision, not a metric)
limitations: by design, to avoid leakage/circularity; means VALID group boundaries were never checked against the VALID distribution's own natural breakpoints.

statement: Only 30.6% of eligible TRAIN images (and 37.3% of eligible VALID images) keep the same complexity group under all 7 tested alternative weighting schemes.
data_source: config/complexity_protocol_snapshot_pp1_v1.json (TRAIN); f25_sensitivity_amendment_report.md Section 2 (VALID, independently re-derived in this session: 132/354 exact match)

limitations: the complexity grouping used for every downstream F2.3-F2.5 result is weight-sensitive for roughly 2/3 of images; group membership should be read as provisional, not a fixed ground truth.

statement: A 30-image AI-vs-algorithm complexity reconciliation sample showed 66.7% exact agreement, Cohen's kappa 0.50.
metric_definition: exact label agreement / weighted & unweighted Cohen's kappa
limitations: n=30, intentionally-selected (not random) sample; 'AI' reviewer is not a domain QC expert; not extrapolatable to the full calibration.

statement: The complexity protocol has NEVER received human-expert (QC) validation; status remains 'human_expert_validation_pending', is_active=false, is_final=false.
metric_definition: n/a
limitations: This applies to every complexity-stratified claim in this package without exception.

statement: The 60-image primary XAI sample is 20/20/20 across Simple/Moderate/High, drawn from 60 distinct source families, containing 92 GT instances.
metric_definition: stratified seeded sample (seed=357), 1 family per group slot, greedy class-coverage pass then seeded order
limitations: candidate pool was family-deduplicated (one representative image per source family); sample is NOT a simple random sample of VALID.

statement: Of 92 GT instances in the sample, 66 were matched to a detector prediction at IoU>=0.5 (26 unmatched); of the 66 matched, 65 produced a valid paired Grad-CAM/Grad-CAM++ explanation (1 Grad-CAM-only failure).
metric_definition: same-class IoU>=0.5 greedy matching; paired success = both methods produced a usable heatmap for the same target/layer
limitations: per-group match rate is NOT uniform: Simple 80.0%, Moderate 79.4%, High 57.6% -- High group has by far the most missingness (see SEL-01).

statement: Matching (detection-availability) rate differs sharply by complexity group: Simple 20/25=80.0%, Moderate 27/34=79.4%, High 19/33=57.6%.
metric_definition: n_matched/n_total per group
limitations: the High group's lower match rate is itself likely complexity-related (harder detections), which means the 65-paired analysis pool is NOT a random subsample of the 92-instance design sample within High -- a selection-bias confound on top of the complexity-weighting confound.

statement: In the High group, the 'cut' defect class drops from 13 instances (92-instance design pool) to 4 (65-instance paired pool); 'gray stitch' drops from 1 to 0 (vanishes entirely).
metric_definition: instance count per class per group, pre- vs post-matching
limitations: any High-group XAI result is therefore not representative of 'cut' or 'gray stitch' defects, which is itself a confound additional to complexity.

statement: Grad-CAM++ has higher instance-pooled pointing accuracy than Grad-CAM overall (33.8% vs 21.5%).
metric_definition: hits/valid_n, hit = GT-box-aligned point falls in method's top activation region
effect_estimate: instance-pooled: +12.3 pp; family-first bootstrap diff: -0.1571 (Grad-CAM minus Grad-CAM++, i.e. Grad-CAM++ higher)
limitations: the family-aware CI crosses zero -- this difference is NOT robust at the family level despite the instance-pooled gap looking large; must not be reported as a confirmed effect.

statement: Grad-CAM++ has higher GT-box energy concentration than Grad-CAM overall (0.249 vs 0.136 instance-pooled; family-first 0.295 vs 0.160).
metric_definition: fraction of total heatmap activation energy inside the matched GT box
limitations: robust at the family level under the baseline (equal-weight) grouping; see CAL-03 for weighting-grouping sensitivity and LOC-04 for the Simple-group exception.

statement: The energy-concentration advantage for Grad-CAM++ is directionally consistent across all 7 alternative weighting schemes in the Moderate and High groups.
metric_definition: instance-pooled energy_fraction_mean per scheme x group x method
n_families: varies by scheme (11-20 families per cell)
effect_estimate: consistent direction in Moderate/High (7/7 schemes each)
ci_95: not computed per-scheme (direction-consistency only; CI-per-scheme not computed for this specific comparison)
limitations: direction-consistency across schemes is a DIFFERENT claim from 'CI excludes zero' -- only the baseline-grouping CI (LOC-02) has been bootstrapped; the 7-scheme figures here are instance-pooled point estimates only.

statement: In the Simple group under the BASELINE (equal-weight) grouping, Grad-CAM has HIGHER energy concentration than Grad-CAM++ (0.134 vs 0.086), the opposite of the overall-pooled direction; this Grad-CAM-favoring direction holds in 5 of 7 alternative weighting schemes and flips to favor Grad-CAM++ only under the 2 luminance-emphasizing schemes.
data_source: alternative_group_metric_summary.csv, scheme=baseline_equal/alt_A/alt_B/alt_C/extreme_*, group=Simple (recomputed directly in this session)
metric_definition: instance-pooled energy_fraction_mean, gradcam vs gradcampp, Simple group only
effect_estimate: 5/7 schemes favor Grad-CAM in Simple; 2/7 (alt_A_emphasise_luminance, extreme_luminance_only) favor Grad-CAM++
limitations: this is the key caveat on LOC-02/LOC-03: the overall pooled energy-concentration advantage for Grad-CAM++ is NOT uniform across complexity groups -- it is driven by Moderate/High and is actually reversed (favoring Grad-CAM) in the Simple group under the grouping used for every other F2.5 result.

statement: Insertion and deletion AUCs are similar between Grad-CAM and Grad-CAM++ (insertion 0.435 vs 0.452; deletion 0.448 vs 0.455).
metric_definition: AUC of class-score vs. fraction of pixels inserted/deleted in heatmap-ranked order, vs. a shared random-pixel-order baseline (0.530)
n_families: 48 (family bootstrap CIs computed but overlap substantially)
ci_95: not a clean exclude/include-zero result for either metric
limitations: small, inconsistently-signed differences; this does NOT establish a robust universal faithfulness advantage for either method and must not be described as 'equivalent faithfulness' (the brief's requested exact phrasing is avoided; see FINDINGS doc).

statement: Grad-CAM has substantially higher stability (robustness to small image perturbations) than Grad-CAM++ under the frozen v1 metric: 0.906 vs 0.303 (overall, baseline grouping).
data_source: xai_evaluation/f24_full_v1/metrics/stability.csv (recomputed directly: gradcam mean=0.9058 n=385, gradcampp mean=0.3028 n=386)
metric_definition: mean Spearman rank correlation between a heatmap and its 6-perturbation-image counterpart
limitations: robust at the baseline grouping, family level. A v2 degenerate-heatmap-aware re-check (stability_v2_degenerate_flagged.csv) WIDENS the Grad-CAM mean slightly (0.9058->0.9110) and leaves Grad-CAM++ unaffected -- the gap is not an artifact of 2 pathological near-empty Grad-CAM heatmaps found in a 9-instance pilot audit.

statement: The Grad-CAM stability advantage over Grad-CAM++ is directionally positive AND has a family-level 95% CI excluding zero in all 21 of 21 scheme x group cells of the F2.5-S1 weighting-sensitivity analysis.
data_source: complexity_xai_analysis/f25_sensitivity_amendment_v1/alternative_group_metric_summary.csv, metric=stability_v1_mean_similarity, method=gap_gradcam_minus_gradcampp (recomputed directly: 21/21 positive point estimate, 21/21 CI excludes zero)
metric_definition: family-first bootstrap of the paired per-instance Grad-CAM-minus-Grad-CAM++ stability_v1 gap, 2000 resamples, seed=357, per each of 7 schemes x 3 groups
effect_estimate: point estimates range 0.35-0.66 across cells; all 21 CIs exclude zero
ci_95: all 21 individually computed, see Table C
limitations: this uses stability_v1 ONLY -- F2.5-S1 did not run a v2-based 7-scheme analysis (confirmed by direct column inspection; see f26_stability_v1_v2_scope_clarification.json). Do not cite this as 'v2-validated'.

statement: Target layer (P3/model.model[15], P4/model.model[18], P5/model.model[21]) composition differs by complexity group in the 65-paired pool; only 2 within-layer group-pair comparisons (P4 Simple-vs-Moderate, P5 Moderate-vs-High) meet the >=5-family-per-side exploratory threshold.
metric_definition: families per group x layer cell, >=5-family-per-side rule for a valid pairwise group comparison
limitations: 5 of 9 individual group x layer cells independently have >=5 families, but a valid BETWEEN-GROUP comparison additionally requires both sides of the pair to clear the threshold simultaneously -- only 2 pairs do. Any complexity-group difference could instead (or additionally) be a target-layer effect.

statement: Only 1 defect class (stain) has >=2 complexity groups (Simple, Moderate) each with >=5 families in the 65-paired pool, so only 1 within-class complexity comparison meets the exploratory threshold.
metric_definition: families per group x class cell, >=5-family-per-side rule
limitations: defect-class is heavily confounded with complexity group in this sample (e.g. 'cut'/'selvet' concentrate in High); complexity effects cannot be cleanly separated from defect-class effects.

statement: The data do not permit a reliable, causally-isolated complexity effect: group assignment is weight-sensitive (CAL-03), matching/selection rates differ sharply by group (SEL-01/SEL-02), target layer and defect class both covary with group (CONF-01/CONF-02), and only a minority of layer/class cells have enough families for even an exploratory pairwise comparison.
data_source: synthesis of CAL-03, SEL-01, SEL-02, CONF-01, CONF-02

limitations: no causal complexity effect is claimed or should be inferred from this package; all complexity-stratified results are descriptive/exploratory only.
classification: unsupported (as a causal claim) / descriptive (as an association)
